articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License for International Development Bank for Investment and Finance
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Iran General License FF-1. This amended general license authorizes the wind-down of transactions involving the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.
This action is part of OFAC's ongoing efforts to manage sanctions against Iran, allowing for an orderly cessation of certain financial activities.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities for North Korea IT Worker Schemes and DRC-Related Activities
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has sanctioned 10 individuals and one entity for their involvement in Democratic People's Republic of Korea (DPRK) government-run information technology (IT) worker schemes. These schemes defraud U.S. businesses and generate revenue for the DPRK's unlawful weapons of mass destruction (WMD) and ballistic missile programs.

Among those designated are Russian nationals Vitold Viktorovich Obertas and Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov, who facilitated millions of dollars in cryptocurrency conversions for DPRK officials and IT agencies. North Korean nationals Kim Ki Hyok and Kim Hyo Dong were also sanctioned for managing DPRK IT worker delegations in Russia.
Additionally, OFAC announced Democratic Republic of the Congo-related designations, though specific details of these designations were not immediately available in the initial announcement.

articles.headline: OFAC Reaches Settlement Agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. for Russia Sanctions Violations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced a settlement agreement with Extreme Networks, Inc. for apparent violations of the Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations. The settlement amount is $1,529,685.

The violations involved transactions with a Russian missile and air defense manufacturer that was deemed a blocked person due to its majority owner being a designated entity, even though the manufacturer itself was not directly on the SDN List at the time of the transactions.

Extreme Networks voluntarily self-disclosed the nine apparent violations and has agreed to maintain a sanctions compliance program for at least five years, including enhanced screening and training measures.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Frequently Asked Questions Regarding Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports

This update is part of OFAC's ongoing process to review and ensure that its published guidance remains current and provides clarity to the public on compliance obligations.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related and Russia-Related General Licenses, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued new Iran General License GG and Iran General License HH. These licenses authorize wind-down activities, limited safety and environmental transactions, and the offloading of cargo involving certain persons or vessels blocked on October 21, 2026, as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast' targeting Iran's shadow fleet network.

Additionally, OFAC issued Russia-related General License 131K, authorizing certain transactions for the negotiation of and entry into contingent contracts for the sale of Lukoil International GmbH and related maintenance activities.

OFAC also announced the removal of two individuals and two entities from the Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List. Belarusian national Andrei Alekseevich Rybakov was delisted under the Belarus sanctions program, and Chinese national Lu Hezheng along with two China-based animation studios were delisted under the North Korea sanctions program.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) Designations and Associated General Licenses
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA). These designations are accompanied by the issuance of associated General Licenses.

Specifically, OFAC issued PAIPA-related General License 1, which generally authorizes transactions prohibited under PAIPA to the extent they are authorized or exempt under the Cyber-related Sanctions Regulations. General License 2 authorizes wind-down activities for certain entities designated on October 19, 2026, until January 19, 2027.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-Related General License for Earthquake Relief Efforts
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued an amended Venezuela-related General License (GL 60A). This license authorizes transactions related to earthquake relief efforts in Venezuela.

GL 60A replaces and supersedes GL 60, extending the authorization period from its original end date of October 23, 2026, to April 21, 2027. Venezuela-related FAQ 1263 was also amended to reflect this extended authorization.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran-Related and Cuba Designations, New and Amended General Licenses and FAQs
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has announced new Iran-related designations and a Cuba designation. These actions are accompanied by the issuance of new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions.

While specific details of the designations were not immediately available in the initial announcement, these actions underscore OFAC's continued focus on both the Iranian and Cuban sanctions programs.

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Jorge Rodriguez from Venezuela-Related Sanctions List
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has removed Jorge Rodriguez, the head of Venezuela's National Assembly, from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list. This action lifts associated asset freezes and removes obstacles for U.S. persons dealing with him.

Rodriguez, who has served as President of Venezuela's National Assembly since 2021, was initially designated in 2018. His delisting comes amid a renewed push for diplomacy and expansion of energy investment between the U.S. and Venezuela.

This move is part of a broader shift in U.S. policy towards Venezuela, following the capture of Nicolás Maduro in January 2026 and the U.S. recognition of acting President Delcy Rodríguez as head of state in March.

articles.headline: OFAC Announces Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations

These designations target individuals and entities involved in illicit drug trafficking and terrorism financing, reinforcing the U.S. government's commitment to disrupting these global threats.

articles.headline: US and Russia Discussing Sanctions Relief for Russian Sovereign Wealth Fund
body: The Trump administration and the Kremlin are reportedly discussing the possible lifting of U.S. sanctions on Russia's multibillion-dollar sovereign wealth fund, the Russian Direct Investment Fund (RDIF).

Russian President Vladimir Putin's foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov stated that talks with the United States to lift sanctions on RDIF have been ongoing for some time. RDIF's CEO, Kirill Dmitriev, is actively engaging American officials on the matter.

The Biden administration initially imposed sanctions on RDIF in February 2022, labeling it a 'known slush fund' for Putin and his inner circle. This discussion comes amidst ongoing negotiations to end the war in Ukraine.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks, Inc. Pays $1,529,685 OFAC Civil Penalty
body: Extreme Networks, Inc. has paid a civil penalty of $1,529,685 to the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC). This settlement resolves apparent violations of OFAC sanctions regulations.
The penalty stems from transactions involving a Russian missile and air defense manufacturer that was considered a blocked person due to its ownership by a designated entity.

OFAC noted mitigating factors including no prior enforcement action and substantial remedial measures taken by Extreme Networks. A portion of the OFAC penalty, $487,861, was deemed satisfied by payments under a parallel Department of Justice non-prosecution agreement.

articles.headline: UN Security Council Debates Iran Sanctions Expiry and Nuclear Program

A representative cited resolution GOV/2026/61 passed by the IAEA Board of Governors on September 9, 2026, emphasizing that legal obligations cannot be unilaterally suspended. Iran was encouraged to clarify outstanding safeguards questions and provide the IAEA with necessary information and access.
The debate underscored the international community's ongoing concerns regarding Iran's nuclear activities and the challenges in ensuring full compliance with international safeguards.

These actions are used to deter, encourage correction of, or prevent violations, unsafe or unsound practices, or breaches of fiduciary duty.

Significant actions include a Cease and Desist Order and a $350 million Civil Money Penalty against American Express National Bank for deficiencies in its Bank Secrecy Act (BSA) compliance program, failure to timely file suspicious activity reports, and customer due diligence and identification program violations.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
